faq.q: Does a well log establish that the water is safe to drink today?
faq.a: No. A drilling or construction record and a current water-quality laboratory result answer different questions. Ask a qualified professional to interpret what the actual records and tests establish.

faq.q: Where can a Texas seller look for an older well report?
faq.a: TCEQ directs owners to Texas Water Development Board data, its Water Well Report Viewer and potentially the local groundwater district. Matching a nearby map point is not enough; verify that a record belongs to the actual well.

faq.q: Who handles testing for a private household well?
faq.a: TCEQ places responsibility for regular testing on the private well owner and recommends an accredited drinking-water laboratory. Ask the laboratory or qualified professional about the appropriate scope and sampling instructions.

faq.q: Can I ask about an as-is sale before replacing well equipment?
faq.a: You can request a Cash As-Is evaluation and describe the known condition and missing information. A proposal does not certify water quality or waive applicable information duties; buyer and closing requirements still need review.
